items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: Oprah said, “Weren’t you afraid she is going to miss a note?”

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Um hum. I can’t brag but when people heard me when I was younger, some people were touched, other people like Leonard Feather said I sounded like a wet noodle one day, so it could have hurt my feelings. But like when I play “Over the Rainbow” for example, a lot of times people cry. I’ve never cried that I remember for Charlie Parker. I mean, these are the great, and Coltrane. The only other time I’ve cried, to be honest, and I won’t go into a big thing about this because my wife would, I don’t want to…

Ellen show. And Ellen said, “Everybody get out your handkerchiefs.” And she was moved. She’s like five foot one, ninety-one pounds, and she sang and she got a standing ovation. She came over with her mother, from the Philippines. And she was crying after she finished, because she got a standing ovation. She had a very rough life. A year later she got a thirteen million dollar deal through David Foster who is the Hit Man, he’s got fifteen gold records. And he had heard of her. He became her stepfather. She toured.…
and cry because I’m gay and no one knew. Like I wasn’t ready to tell people.” I mean it just breaks my heart.
